method: Assistant opened each listed original PNG using view_image; written observations are separate from PNG statistics and actual draw validation. No pixels edited.

observations: The original building geometry, street depth, lane layout, skyline and camera composition are visibly retained.
The right stone walk reads as a cooler grey mineral surface instead of the previous cream tone. Daytime change is modest; existing signs and thin practical fittings remain visible.
Large sealed ground windows remain deliberately simple and the far skyline is still a repeated stepped silhouette. This frame is not a wholesale facade realism transformation.
Same street lamps and sky background remain at the same exposure. The bright sidewalk bands are visibly darker and more readable as paving; the street remains lit by several overlapping warm pools.
Sparse upper lit windows are visible above the ground storey. The storefronts and their brackets remain discernible; road reflections are present in the genuine WebGL frame.

Some near vertical facade patches are still very bright, while the upper storeys and several near pockets remain dark. The parked car is primarily a small dark silhouette in this particular fixed view. No full-city night-lighting or hardware FPS verdict follows.

The 18 m boulevard now has two clear traffic lanes in each direction, with lane marks ending before cross streets. The grey mineral forecourts are distinct from the asphalt instead of the old continuous tarmac expanse.
Existing tree/seat kits visibly mark both street edges at a human scale; the skyline, viaduct and original building positions remain recognisably the same.

Both sides still have broad sparsely occupied forecourts, repeat rectangular tower forms and a simple smooth distant hill silhouette. The improvement does not remove the city's simplified construction.
Warm lit panes and dim ground-storey glazing now make the large tower positions and storey rhythms legible where the baseline was almost wholly dark.
The bright near road pool and successive light pools remain, while the added lane markings clarify the broad carriageway. The sky exposure is retained.

Tree/bench kits and the large side forecourts remain low contrast in this night camera. Most of the high-rise mass is still very dark; sparse emissive panes are not a complete physical facade illumination solution.
Actual final refreshed wet-road FBO has 171 draw calls including all five previously failing asphalt draws, with no GL errors; this observation is separate from the image quality judgement.
The left foreground and far road edges now distinguish grey-green mineral forecourts from the continuous inherited asphalt. Extra lane marks reach the junction without covering its crossing.
The existing crosswalk, directional arrows, viaduct, ramp and building parcels are preserved. There is no camera or global exposure change masking the difference.
The intersection is still very broad and sparsely furnished; large dark boxlike facades and the exposed diagonal ramp remain prominent.

Warm glazing now identifies the central block and the right-hand towers and their ground storeys instead of near-black masses. The crosswalk and turn arrows remain illuminated by an actual bounded lamp pool.

The near walk is darker than the original bright strip. The far left cross road has a separate cool light patch; multiple layers of light are present rather than relying on a visible vehicle headlight.

The foreground beyond the near pool, much of the forecourt and the viaduct remain very dark. The warm window pattern improves orientation but does not complete the underlying facade or skyline detail.
The original maintenance court, steel portal, WORK BAY sign, slab seams and inner curb remain visible and essentially unchanged under the matched sun.

This camera is south of the actual navigation vehicle entrance and is not evidence that the car reached it. It shows retained bay geometry, with no substantial new art improvement claimed for the court itself.
Large plain closed wall panels remain prominent and the far backing structure is simple; a road-lighting improvement cannot be inferred from this daylight courtyard alone.
The distant tower now has visible warm panes and the WORK BAY sign remains readable. That is the main visible improvement in this particular camera.

The working-court floor and adjacent closed wall panels are still almost entirely dark. This fixed view does not establish satisfactory courtyard night illumination or arrival at the navigation endpoint.
This retained limitation is not hidden by brightening the exposure or substituting a different camera.
The original upper-road connection, guardrails and elevated street geometry remain at the same angle and scale. The new low rail fixture is visible on its real support at the right foreground.
Ground-storey modules behind the junction add limited entrance rhythm, but the broad unoccupied paved area and repeated rectangular facades remain apparent.
The guardrail fixture and the stationary image do not show the vehicle actually traversing the original ramp.

The physically mounted low rail fixture now lights the immediate road/rail region; it was nearly invisible in the baseline. Lit upper panes and several distant ground-level fixtures make building layers easier to distinguish.

The nearby fixture is strongly clipped and its bloom looks blocky at this distance. Large sections of the upper junction remain dark beyond the local pool. These are retained visual limits, not a photometric or AAA-quality pass.
This is a fixed camera at the connection, not evidence of complete native ascent or continuous illumination of the full upper route.

This is the main running city renderer in cockpit mode, not the separate inspection environment. The windscreen frames a visible street, sky, footbridge, directional sign and shopfronts across the upper part of the image.
The left A-pillar, door cap, steering yoke, dashboard and central screen are actual visible cabin geometry. They no longer replace the upper view with an undifferentiated black region.

The dashboard and screen remain simplified, with dark instrument surfaces and a broad pillar in this eye position. This image checks a usable forward view, not OEM interior detail or instrument ergonomics.
frames.scope: Final main-city renderer; no matched old cockpit is newly asserted.

observations: The main-scene cabin receives warm street-light response on the A-pillar, door cap and dashboard; the road beyond the windscreen remains readable.
The white headlamp pool is visible together with separate warm storefront and canopy lighting, overhead wayfinding and distant facade windows. The upper half is the real street/sky view.
The cabin material treatment is still stylized and a few fine bright speckles are visible on interior edges; this is not a claim of final automotive material or anti-aliasing quality.
frames.scope: Final main-city renderer; no matched old cockpit is newly asserted.

reviewScope: Ten matched original 3.15 / final 3.16 pairs and two final main-scene cockpit originals were individually opened and visually reviewed. The matrix remains a separate attempt and is not passed by these images.
matchedConditionComparison: Camera position/quaternion/projection, resolution, physical vehicle state, pause, weather, quality and locked exposure agree within 1e-9 for each of the ten pairs. Wall-clock time and decorative animation are not synchronized.

drawReview.scope: Every final same-frame JSON was checked for complete draw attribution, all expected categories, program/FBO validity and per-draw GL errors. This is separate from the visual observations above.

wetReflectionRefresh.actualTarget: Wet road / bounded linear specular capture
wetReflectionRefresh.scope: The actual capture includes writes into the reflection FBO, so it is not a cached-texture-only frame.

matrixAttempts.failureScope: First ordinary frame completed 1,209 draw calls. The following request for a complete export draw and PNG exceeded the original 20 s deadline, which starts when queued, before the export draw. The original report retains only the preceding ordinary partialAudit. It does not isolate which export phase consumed the time.
matrixAttempts.laterAttempt: The separately preserved unchanged 800x450 protocol completed four original frames and then also failed its application deadline. Neither attempt passes the 14-frame matrix.

matrixAttempts.failureScope: The fifth complete export request exceeded the unchanged application 20 s deadline after its preceding ordinary frame passed. This is an application deadline, not an automation download timeout. Failed-export phase data was unavailable in this build.
matrixAttempts.schedulerFollowup: The separate 28e9bc41 original 1280x720 matrix completed 14/14 images and 28 clean ordinary/export audits under the original 20s request deadline. All fourteen original PNGs were individually opened. The 81926 failed prefix remains unchanged.

bounds: These are actual Chrome 155 WebGL2 / ANGLE SwiftShader frames; no hardware GPU performance is inferred.
Original baseline wet-road draw errors remain intact in the same-frame reports. Its visible PNGs do not establish a clean original GPU path.
The final fixed Foundry work-bay camera is south of the actual [100,0,315] navigation endpoint; no native arrival is established by it.
The final terrace image is a fixed upper-connection view, not a completed ascent.
No whole-city AAA, photographic realism, stable moving-frame coverage or human driving-feel verdict is made.
The Foundry court remains underlit; broad boulevard forecourts, repeated distant boxes, simplified hills and a clipped rail light remain visible limitations.

independentCockpitReview.reviewerRole: Vehicle specialist agent; offline original PNG review, no additional browser session
observations: The upper half of the actual main-scene cockpit image contains the street, overhead structure and sky. Door top, A-pillar, wheel and dashboard remain readable.
Wet-night warm lighting reaches the interior while the headlamp foreground pool and facade lights remain separately visible.
The interior remains a simplified model: the right schematic display is large, control details and steering-wheel edges are coarse. This is not an OEM-production-interior claim.

currentDiagnosticMatrix.scope: New source-bound matrix; the prior twelve fixed-city originals retain their actual 81926 capture identity.
